title: Tissue clearing: seeing in 3D
objective: Explain what tissue clearing does and when it beats thin sections.

steps.title: Why tissue is opaque
steps.body: Tissue scatters light because lipids and proteins bend light more than the water around them, so light bends at every membrane. **[[tissue clearing|Tissue clearing]]** (e.g. CLARITY, iDISCO) removes or index-matches those components so a whole block turns transparent — then you can image deep without slicing.

steps.prompt: What is the main point of clearing a sample?
options: To make a thick, intact sample transparent for 3D imaging
To fix the tissue far faster than paraformaldehyde can
To chemically amplify weak antibody signals in the tissue
To freeze tissue solid without forming damaging ice crystals
steps.explanation: Clearing matches refractive index so light passes through intact tissue, enabling 3D imaging of whole structures.

variants.setup: You clear an intact piece of tissue before imaging.
variants.prompt: What does clearing let you do?
options: Image deep into an intact 3D sample
Image living tissue without fixing it
Count single mRNA dots without probes
variants.reveal: A cleared block is transparent, so a confocal or light-sheet scope can image through its full depth.

steps.setup: You want to trace a single afferent's full arbor through a thick piece of gut wall.
steps.prompt: What do you predict clearing + 3D imaging buys you?
options: A continuous 3D view of the whole arbor in a single sample
A sharper surface image, while deeper parts stay hazy
Brighter labeling, since clearing amplifies the fluorophore
steps.reveal: Clearing lets you image the intact arbor in 3D, avoiding the error-prone job of stitching it back together from serial sections.

variants.prompt: Clearing a whole-mount tissue mainly helps you…
options: Avoid stitching an arbor back from many thin sections
Fix the tissue noticeably faster than immersion would
Replace the need for any antibody or fluorescent label
variants.explanation: You image the intact 3D structure directly instead of reconstructing it.

steps.title: The catch
steps.body: Clearing is slower, needs compatible labels (some clearing chemistries quench fluorophores), and demands a scope that can image deep (confocal or light-sheet, C9). It's a tool for *whole-structure* questions, not every stain.

flag.note: Many clearing methods exist (CLARITY, iDISCO, CUBIC…) with different chemistries and trade-offs.

sources.note: CLARITY tissue clearing for intact-tissue imaging.
